$comment: npm-audit equivalent of .trivyignore, consumed by scripts/npm-audit-gate.mjs (the blocking Security Scan step). Every entry needs an advisory id, the tree it applies to (scope = npm prefix, or '*'), a reason, an added date, and an expires date. 🔴 expires is ENFORCED as of 2026-08-28: past its date the entry stops suppressing and the advisory blocks again, because a review cadence written only in prose is how a suppression list becomes permanent. Expiring does not mean the advisory is fixed — it means a human undertook to look again by then. Re-justify with a new date, or remove the entry.

exceptions.reason: image-size ICNS-parser DoS. npm reports the vulnerable range as '*' — EVERY published version is affected, so there is no version to upgrade to (1.2.1 is the last of the 1.x line, published the same day upstream moved to 2.0.2, and 2.x is not fixed either). npm's only offered 'fix' is react-native 0.72.17, flagged isSemVerMajor — a major DOWNGRADE from 0.81.5 that would break the app without fixing the flaw. Reachable only via metro, the Expo/React-Native dev bundler (@expo/metro, @react-native/community-cli-plugin): it reads image dimensions while building the JS bundle on a developer machine or CI runner, does not ship in the compiled APK/IPA, and never runs on a server. The images it parses are the repo's own committed assets, not untrusted input. Same reachability class as the undici/ws and image-size CVE entries in .trivyignore. Remove as soon as upstream publishes a fixed image-size that metro accepts.

image-size JXL/HEIF-parser DoS — same package, same vulnerable range '*', same dev-bundler-only reachability and same absent fix as GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr above; see that entry for the full reasoning. Remove both together when a fixed image-size ships.
